title: Restrict user consent for apps and AI tools
problem: Employees grant third-party AI tools access to mail and files via OAuth consent.
steps: Entra admin center > Entra ID > Enterprise apps > Consent and permissions > User consent settings.
Select 'Allow user consent for apps from verified publishers, for selected permissions' or 'Do not allow user consent'.
Enable the admin consent workflow (Admin consent settings) so users can request access.
pitfalls: Existing grants remain — review them separately.
Changing the setting in the portal needs Global Administrator; via Graph PowerShell a Privileged Role Administrator is enough.
done_when: User consent is set to 'Do not allow' or to verified publishers with selected permissions.
The admin consent workflow is enabled, with reviewers assigned.

sources.title: Configure how users consent to applications

troubleshooting.symptom: Users are blocked from an app they need.
troubleshooting.fix: Expected after restricting consent. They request it through the admin consent workflow; review and grant admin consent for that app.

troubleshooting.symptom: Users can't request access at all.
troubleshooting.cause: The admin consent workflow isn't enabled or has no reviewers.
troubleshooting.fix: Enable it under Admin consent settings and assign reviewers.

troubleshooting.symptom: Risky apps still have access after the change.
troubleshooting.fix: Review and revoke existing permission grants separately.

rollback: Enterprise apps > Consent and permissions > User consent settings: return to the previously used option (record it before you change). Needs Global Administrator in the portal; Graph PowerShell works with Privileged Role Administrator.
Prefer moving from 'Do not allow' to 'verified publishers, selected permissions' over reopening full user consent.
Confirm by having a test user attempt consent to an allowed app.
